title: Redesign platform-binary release provenance to build-fresh-in-CI, never commit to git (like lore-cli)
description:
Filed while diagnosing QCLI-258's release-commit blocker (an OOM committing ~493MB of six platform binaries). The orchestrator, comparing quest-cli's .git (1.0GB, packed size 831.67 MiB per `git count-objects -vH`) against lore-cli's (10.7MB, ~55x smaller), asked whether the binaries need to be committed to git at all.

Answer established by reading release.yml, prepublication-qualification.yml, and scripts/qualification/native-execution-receipt.mjs directly (not the runbook alone): YES, under the CURRENT architecture. release.yml's Publish step does not rebuild -- it runs `npm publish` straight from `npm/quest-${target}` as committed at the release ref. That is gated by `native-execution-receipt.mjs --verify-committed`, which asserts (a) `git hash-object` of the on-disk binary equals the blob committed at that exact ref, and (b) its sha256 matches package.json's `questPlatformPackages` manifest. Bun's `--compile` output is not byte-reproducible, so today git-blob equality is the ONLY mechanism proving "the bytes CI attested to are the bytes that get published" (QCLI-135's fail-closed design).

lore-cli, asked directly, confirmed the alternative is real: they have never committed a single binary byte (`git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'npm/*/bin/lore*'` returns zero hits, per ADR-0001). `npm/*/bin/` is gitignored; only tiny per-platform package.json templates are committed; release.yml builds each platform fresh and publishes straight from the freshly-built tarball -- the binary bytes never touch git, not even transiently.

Quest's own CI already has both halves of that pattern, just not wired to the publish path: `immutable-candidates` already builds fresh via `bun run build:packages` on non-tag refs (not from a committed binary), and `candidate-bundle` already flows freshly-built artifacts job-to-job via upload/download-artifact with zero git involvement, for `workflow_dispatch`. What's missing to match lore-cli: extend that same artifact-flow to the tag/publish job itself, and rework the receipt to attest "this CI run built this artifact from this exact commit" instead of "git contains this exact blob."

This is a genuine redesign of the native-execution-receipt's trust boundary (QCLI-135), not a small tweak: opum-cli-e2e's validator reads this receipt shape, and lore-cli's own release pattern is the reference implementation to align with. System-boundary enough to warrant a lore ADR before implementation, per the SDLC skill's own rule.

Sizing, for context: current working tree's npm/ (six 0.6.0 binaries) is 497MB; total .git is 1.0GB (208MB loose + 832MB packed). Roughly half of .git is the current version's binaries; the other roughly-equal half is superseded binaries from past releases (0.3.0 through 0.5.0) still sitting in packed history near their original size, since compiled binaries do not delta-compress against each other. Every release compounds this -- it is not one bloated commit. A history rewrite could recover several hundred MB but is explicitly out of scope here (reserved for the user's own direct authorization, tracked separately as part of the public-repo audit).

Not started. Filed for scheduling, not to be picked up proactively.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An ADR (or equivalent design note) exists proposing the build-fresh-in-CI, never-commit-to-git architecture for platform binaries, reviewed jointly with lore-cli (whose current release.yml is the reference implementation) and opum-cli-e2e (whose receipt validator reads the current --verify-committed shape and would need to accept a new attestation mode)

The proposed redesign specifies exactly how native-execution-receipt.mjs's trust mechanism changes from asserting git-blob equality to asserting artifact provenance from a specific CI run and commit, without weakening QCLI-135's fail-closed guarantee against publishing unattested bytes

A decision is recorded on whether npm/quest-*/bin/* stays committed for any transitional period, or moves to gitignored on adoption, and how the changeover is sequenced across a release boundary without leaving a release unable to publish

implementationNotes: Correction from opum-agent, relayed here since it changes this task's scope: the fresh native-execution receipt produced at v0.6.0/ce551cf (QCLI-258 AC#3) does NOT flip opum-cli-e2e's 6 stale-committed-receipt FAIL rows in 50-packaging. opum-cli-e2e tested it directly (bound via --quest-receipt, re-ran 50-packaging): same 40 PASS / 6 FAIL / 1 BLOCKED. Those 6 rows read a hardcoded committed path (evidence/native-receipts/quest-01456d7-native-receipts.json) in opum-cli-e2e's own repo, unconditionally -- --quest-receipt only feeds a separate three-way-corroboration row, with no live path to bind a fresh receipt into those 6 rows at all. That is opum-cli-e2e's own design, not a quest-cli-side gap. Implication: build-fresh-in-CI (this task's proposal) is NOT sufficient on its own to close that gap -- opum-cli-e2e also needs its own change to read a bound receipt instead of a committed path, which is a genuine cross-repo dependency. opum-agent has told opum-cli-e2e to file that plumbing gap in its own tracker; reference that task here once it exists rather than assuming the fix is entirely inside quest-cli. Also: the 6 FAILs are NOT demonstrated to be non-defects -- opum-cli-e2e could not verify the fresh receipt's digests against the locally-built binary because nothing currently reads it, so cite them as 'the plumbing gap, precisely located,' not as proof the binaries are fine.
